summary: Pend Oreille County, WA tower built 1930 (40-ft L-4); taken down in 1935 per three sources, though firelookout.com says abandoned in the 1940s; no remains described.

facts.design: 40-foot pole tower with an L-4 cab; a tent cabin and a patrol tower stood half a mile northeast
facts.status_note: Register and firelookout.com say it is gone; no source describes what, if anything, remains on the summit
facts.agency: U.S. Forest Service (Colville National Forest, per the register)

events.note: 40-foot pole tower with L-4 cab on the peak; tent cabin and patrol tower half a mile northeast (register, firelookout.com, Willhite)
Jimmie Monroe struck by lightning at the site, per Willhite; the source does not describe a fire or a staffing role
Register says destroyed in 1935; Willhite and the Forest Lookouts page say the legs were sawn off and the tower pushed over the cliff after the fire season
Firelookout.com says 'Abandoned 1940s'; the year 1940 stands in for the decade only and conflicts with the 1935 account
Registered April 17, 2020 as US 2030, WA 501; nominated by Tammy McLeod

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The register says destroyed in 1935. Willhite and the Forest Lookouts page say that after the 1935 fire season the legs were sawn off and the tower pushed over a cliff. Firelookout.com says abandoned in the 1940s. The 1935 account has three sources; the story reports the 1940s claim as the outlier.
The register and firelookout.com give the Colville National Forest; the Forest Lookouts page gives the Kaniksu National Forest. The story uses Colville and notes the other name.

sources.title: Prouty Peak Lookout Site & Patrol Point on Green Mountain

notes_for_editor: Brief record (built 1930, removed 1935, registered 2020) checks out; no corrections. Access is not described in any source read, so no access key is set. The 1940s abandonment on firelookout.com cannot be dated more closely; the 1940 event year is a placeholder for the decade. Staffing: only Jimmie Monroe's 1933 lightning strike is named, and no source calls him a lookout.
